# Meshery

> The extensible cloud native manager. Confidently wrangle cloud native infrastructure with Meshery.

Meshery is now a CNCF Incubating project.

[Read the announcement](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/10/07/meshery-becomes-a-cncf-incubating-project/)

 × 

[&nbsp;](https://meshery.io/)

# Infrastructure as design, for people and AI agents.

Meshery turns your infrastructure into a shared, relationship-aware model, so every change, whether written by an engineer or suggested by an AI, is visible, validated, and reviewable before it reaches production.

CNCF Incubating - nearly 400 integrations - Kubernetes, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and beyond

[](https://meshery.io/assets/videos/meshery-dashboard-hero-image.webp "Meshery Dashboard")

[Get Started](https://meshery.io/#getting-started)[Try the Playground](https://play.meshery.io)

[See how Meshery grounds AI →](https://meshery.io/#ai-agents)

[](https://github.com/meshery/meshery)[](https://github.com/meshery/meshery)

The problem

## AI writes infrastructure faster than anyone can review it.

### Looks right, fails in production.

Generated YAML passes syntax checks and plans, then breaks on a missing mount, a wrong selector, or an over-broad role.

**Meshery:** validates designs against how components actually relate.

### Knowledge lives in a few heads.

How resources affect one another is tribal knowledge held by senior engineers.

**Meshery:** encodes it in versioned models that every engineer and agent share.

### Tool and team sprawl.

Helm, Kustomize, cloud consoles, and Kubernetes clusters each show a different slice.

**Meshery:** one live model across hundreds of technologies, with workspaces for every team.

## Models that know how your infrastructure fits together.

Meshery models encode expert knowledge of how components relate and how a change to one affects the rest: what mounts what, what selects what, who may talk to whom. Meshery's [policy engine](https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/policies) evaluates every design as it is created, updated, or imported, automatically creating [relationships](https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/relationships) and updating linked configuration when they form or dissolve. Think of it as the senior engineer's mental model, externalized, versioned, and enforceable.

[Explore relationships](https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/relationships)

EdgeHierarchicalSibling

_Example: Kubernetes Deployment with ConfigMap applied_

_Hierarchical - Parent: Namespace (Parent) and ConfigMap (child), Role (Child)_

_Example: Kubernetes Pod with Persistent Volume mounted via Persistent Volume Claim_

_Example: Kubernetes Ingress mapped a Service_

_Example: Kubernetes Cluster Role assigned to a Service Account_

_Example: Kubernetes Service and Deployment with matching label selectors_

Built for AI agents

## Give your AI agents ground truth, and keep humans in control.

Agents should retrieve real components from the Meshery registry instead of inventing them, see live topology through MeshSync, and have their proposed changes validated against relationships and policy before a human approves them.

### Meshery MCP Server

Connect AI assistants and agents to Meshery models, designs, and live state.

### Headless mesheryctl and [mesheryctl-axi](https://github.com/meshery-extensions/mesheryctl-axi)

Agent-friendly, scriptable control of Meshery, from your terminal or from your agent.

### Human oversight

AI-suggested changes become designs that are proposed for review, not deployed by default.

### Visual diffs in pull requests

Reviewers see what a change does to infrastructure, not just lines of YAML.

[Connect your agent](https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-mcp-server)

[mesheryctl reference](https://docs.meshery.io/reference/mesheryctl/)

# Nearly 400 integrations. Far beyond Kubernetes.

Manage Kubernetes and non-Kubernetes infrastructure in one model, including hundreds of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure services, CNCF projects, and the tools you already use. Import existing Helm and Kustomize assets into a single live model that people and AI agents share.

[Show All Integrations](https://meshery.io/#integrations)[View Integrations in 3D](https://meshery.io/integrations)

## Infrastructure as design. Start from proven patterns.

Designs capture the desired state of your infrastructure, components and relationships together, as a reusable, versioned artifact. Start from a catalog pattern, adapt it, validate it, and deploy it, or give it to an agent as a known-good starting point.

[Browse the Catalog](https://meshery.io/catalog)

Integrations

## Collaborative configuration management for every team.

Create as many workspaces as you need to organize designs, environments, and access. Teams review the same design, comment on the same change, and control who can deploy where.

[Learn about Workspaces](https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/workspaces)

  

## Manage your resources with Environments

Environments make it easier for you to manage, share, and work with a collection of resources as a group, instead of dealing with all your connections and credentials on an individual basis.

[View Docs](https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/environments)

## The foundation for your internal developer platform.

Meshery includes both REST APIs and GraphQL APIs, pluggable adapters via gRPCs, hot-loadable ReactJS and hot-loadable Golang binaries. The great number of [extension points](https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility) in Meshery make it ideal as the foundation of your internal developer platform. Package your own models so your organization's rules about how infrastructure fits together are enforced for every engineer and every agent.

[Create your own model](https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-models#instructions-for-creating-a-new-model)

 

## Operate across clusters and clouds

See live state through MeshSync discovery and act on many clusters and cloud accounts from one place.

[View Docs](https://docs.meshery.io/guides/configuration-management)

  

Where Meshery fits

## Works with the tools you already trust.

Keep Terraform, Helm, and GitOps for delivery. Keep your developer portal for ownership. Meshery adds the relationship-aware layer in between: design and validate what should be true before your pipelines ship it.

# Getting Started

## with Meshery

## Using Meshery Playground

The fastest way to put your hands on Meshery is in its playground. No installation required. Just click and go!

[Use Meshery Playground](https://play.meshery.io)

## Using Your Platform Of Choice and Install

Choose a platform and see how easy it is to start managing cloud native infrastructure with a single command.

 Bash User Brew User Docker User Kubernetes User Windows User Google Kubernetes AWS Elastic Kubernetes AKS Minikube Helm 

### Bash using Mac or Linux

Install on Kubernetes

` $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=kubernetes bash - ` Copy to clipboard  

Install on Docker

` $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=docker bash - ` Copy to clipboard  

### Brew User:

Install on Mac or Linux using Homebrew:

` $ brew install mesheryctl
                $ mesheryctl system start` Copy to clipboard  

### Docker User:

#### Get mesheryctl

Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, Scoop, or [download directly](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest).

#### Use mesheryctl

`mesheryctl system context create docker --platform docker --set
                mesheryctl system start` Copy to clipboard  

#### Use Docker Extension for Meshery

`docker extension install meshery/docker-extension-meshery:stable-latest` Copy to clipboard  

### Kubernetes User:

#### Get mesheryctl

Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, Scoop, or [download directly](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest).

#### Use mesheryctl

`mesheryctl system context create k8s --platform kubernetes --set
                mesheryctl system start` Copy to clipboard  

### Windows User:

#### Using Scoop

` $ scoop bucket add mesheryctl https://github.com/meshery/scoop-bucket.git
                        $ scoop install mesheryctl
                        $ mesheryctl system start ` Copy to clipboard  

#### Using Binary

Not a Scoop user? Download and unzip the [mesheryctl](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest) binary directly from the Meshery releases page. Add mesheryctl to your path for ease of use. Then, execute:

` $ mesheryctl system start ` Copy to clipboard  

### Azure Kubernetes Service ( AKS ) User:

#### Get mesheryctl

Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, Scoop, or [download directly](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest).

#### Use mesheryctl

Authenticate to Azure and configure credentials for your intended AKS cluster using `az aks get-credentials --resource-group <resource-group> --name <cluster-name>`. Verify the active context using `kubectl config current-context` and select the intended context using `kubectl config use-context <context-name>` when necessary. Consult the official [AKS setup instructions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/learn/quick-kubernetes-deploy-cli) for more details.

`mesheryctl system start -p kubernetes` Copy to clipboard  

### Minikube User:

#### Get mesheryctl

Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, or Scoop, or [download directly](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest).

#### Use mesheryctl

` mesheryctl system config minikube ` Copy to clipboard  

### Using Helm

`helm repo add meshery https://meshery.io/charts/
              helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --create-namespace` Copy to clipboard  

Learn about [Meshery's Helm charts](https://meshery.io/charts). Don't forget to grab a copy of mesheryctl. Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, or Scoop.

### Google Kubernetes Engine User:

#### Get mesheryctl

Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, or Scoop, or [download directly](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest).

#### Using mesheryctl

Authenticate to Google Cloud and configure credentials for your intended GKE cluster using `gcloud container clusters get-credentials <cluster-name> --location <region-or-zone>`. Verify the active context using `kubectl config current-context` and select the intended context using `kubectl config use-context <context-name>` when necessary. Consult the official [GKE cluster access instructions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-access-for-kubectl) for more details.

`mesheryctl system start -p kubernetes` Copy to clipboard  

### AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service User:

#### Get mesheryctl

Install mesheryctl with Bash, Brew, Scoop, or [download directly](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest).

#### Use mesheryctl

` mesheryctl system config eks
                mesheryctl system start ` Copy to clipboard

Louie Corbo

Staff Cloud Infrastructure Engineer at SADA

> The Meshery Extension transforms Docker Desktop into a powerful load generation utility, conveniently enabling me to deploy and configure any cloud native application with a click of the button and invoke and control load-based performance tests from my desktop.

Maximiliano Churichi

Software Engineer at HPE

> The precision by which performance measurements are generated and analyzed is a pinnacle focus of Nighthawk. Mesh performance characterization should be distilled from a set of value measurements, and that is where MeshMark complements to create the ultimate comprehensive efficiency calculation.

Otto Van Der Schaaf

Principal Engineer at Red Hat

> Meshery is the perfect tool for ensuring that your cloud native applications are optimally configured and performing well; it also gives you a fantastic visual insight into what can be a large amount of textual configuration.

Nic Jackson

Principal Developer Advocate at HashiCorp

> While speed is one of Linkerd's core competitive advantages, Linkerd provides much more than just an ultrafast data plane. We are pleased to support MeshMark's establishment of a higher order set of functional considerations that incorporate value into the performance equation.

William Morgan

CEO of Buoyant and one of the creators of Linkerd

> Performance measurement data rarely provides a clear and simple picture of how well our applications are performing from a business point of view, which are so often the key efficiency indicators that we really need.

Ken Owens

Vice President Cyber Cloud Security Engineering at Fiserv

> Many cloud native adopters have been put off from using service mesh due to the extra resource consumption and complexity that it can involve. We welcome MeshMark as an objective measure of that overhead, to help drive efficiency and make it easier for users to compare service mesh options.

Liz Rice

Chief Open Source Officer, Isovalent and Emeritus Chair of the CNCF's TOC

Kaur Kallas

Software Architect at Entigo

Deepak Dinesh

Meshery User

> Are my resources utilized as best as possible? Why am I not getting the SLO met with 4 resources when I only needed 1 resource without the service mesh? How can I improve my 99.9% latencies or can I map my service policy to utilization? MeshMark will model and provide an index in answer to such questions.

Mrittika Ganguli

Principal Engineer & Director Cloud Native Network Pathfinding
